transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-01-15 14:30 UTC
Duration: 52 minutes
Attendees: Maya (Redwood AE), Ethan (Redwood SE), Aisha (Crescendo Head of Platform), Marco (SRE), Lisa (CISO), Thomas (Prod Dir)

Summary notes (auto): compliance-triggered escalation; customer requires audit artifacts and a concrete fallback plan that preserves data residency and uses KMS; discuss dedicated/private options and immediate mitigations.

[00:00] Maya (Redwood): hi everyone, thanks for hopping on. we got the note from your compliance team yesterday, uh, and wanted to make sure we align on what they asked and what we can ship fast.
[00:18] Aisha (Crescendo): yeah thanks Maya. lisa pushed a red flag after the vendor audit. the auditors want proof of immutable audit logs and a clear plan for degraded operation if KMS access is revoked.
[00:32] Lisa (CISO): to be clear — we need a way to show chain-of-custody for request/response, and retention metadata. also encryption-at-rest with a KMS/HSM we control is a must for our regulator.
[00:47] Ethan (Redwood SE): makes sense. quick clarifier: when you say "KMS we control" are you asking for customer-managed KMS integrated into the private plane, or just evidence of envelope encryption hooks we support?
[01:05] Lisa (CISO): ideally customer-managed in our VPC, yes. the auditors asked for an HSM-backed KEK and attestations.
[01:17] Maya (Redwood): ok noted. we support KMS integrations in Private and Dedicated, and for hosted we have an HSM-managed KMS but not customer key ingress — that difference sometimes trips audits.
[01:35] Thomas (Prod): can you say more about what the hosted behavior is for audit logs? auditors flagged that logs are trimmed after 90 days and that some request metadata is not included.
[01:48] Ethan (Redwood SE): currently hosted retains full traces for 90 days by default; we can export incremental logs on-demand. for the metadata gap — there are a couple fields that are optional in the current export: route origin, model hash, and kv-cache hits. we can enable those for you as an augmentation.

[02:12] Marco (SRE): the main concern is: if your KMS is unreachable or we revoke a key due to a legal hold, what is the graceful fallback so our customer-facing inference remains online but without violating the key mandate?
[02:26] Ethan: good question. typical patterns we see: 1) automatic model-variant fallback to an unencrypted-only inference host (if allowed), 2) degrade to local on-prem variant in your VPC, or 3) route to a read-only cached response layer using prefix/KV cache.
[02:44] Aisha: option 1 feels risky from legal. option 2 requires on-prem infra we don't have. option 3 sounds promising — can you detail the prefix cache idea?
[02:58] Ethan: sure. we have automatic prefix and KV cache — basically we can keep deterministic prefix responses for repeated queries. it can serve most of the common prompts with sub-10ms responses and avoids going back to model if keys are restricted. caveat: not all prompts are cacheable, and you lose freshness.
[03:21] Lisa: auditors will look for proof that cached outputs don't leak PII and that the cache respects retention windows. is cache eviction policy auditable?
[03:34] Maya: yes we can provide cache metadata, eviction logs, and show TTLs. also we can produce a short export demonstrating a cache-only session for a sanitized prompt set.
[03:48] Thomas: cost tradeoffs? caching seems cheaper but what about long-tail queries that bypass cache?
[03:55] Ethan: exactly — caching reduces tokens served and cost, but long-tail queries still go to the model if permitted. during a key-revocation event, a hybrid strategy is to serve cache-only + degrade some endpoints to a lightweight on-device or on-prem model — which increases infra cost but maintains availability.
[04:18] Aisha: Operationally, we need a concrete playbook — auditors want "what do you do step 0..n". can Redwood draft a fallback sprint plan we can run to prove the behavior?
[04:31] Maya: absolutely. proposal: we run a 2-week sprint with goals: a) demonstrate audit log export and retention proof, b) run a bench where KMS is simulated as revoked and measure CDN/KV cache hit-rate and latencies, c) implement a canary fallback route and test end-to-end.
[04:50] Marco: timeline? we prefer this before the compliance board meeting on Feb 10.
[04:57] Maya: feasible — sprint starting Feb 2 gives a week buffer.
[05:03] Lisa: what artifacts do you need from us to start prep?
[05:08] Ethan: sample audit log schema (even anonymized), any regulatory retention requirements (they may ask 7 years etc), and confirmation of which KV entries are considered PII and must be scrubbed.
[05:21] Marco: i'll pull our current retention policy and a sample, but it will be noisy.
[05:27] Aisha: and we will route an NDA addendum to allow Redwood access to a redacted prod subset for the bench.

[05:40] (short silence, typing)
[05:48] Maya: ok while we pull assets, we should talk immediate mitigations you can accept today. we can turn on extended logging and ship a trimmed SOC2 excerpt plus architecture diagram by Monday.
[06:02] Lisa: Monday works. auditors also want to see HSM attestation details; can you provide a vendor attestation for your hosted HSM?
[06:13] Maya: yes we can provide vendor attestation. for customer-managed HSM we have docs on integration.

[06:25] Ethan: slight aside on the log schema — there's sometimes a mismatch between "model hash" and the model manifest name. auditors often want the exact commit or model file checksum. we can include a model artifact checksum in the export.

[06:43] Thomas: perfect. also, is there a way to bind log exports to a signed timestamp to ensure non-repudiation?
[06:50] Ethan: we support signed audit exports with a timestamped signature using our signing service; if you need, we can also route the signature to your KMS for dual-control. that might satisfy the non-repudiation ask.

[07:04] Lisa: what about data residency for those audit exports? auditors want logs to remain in eu data centers. can Redwood export EU-hosted logs only?
[07:15] Maya: yes, we have region-bound exports for EU only — that's available in Dedicated and Private; for Hosted we can generate EU-only exports if the deployment region is EU. we'll include region metadata in the export.

[07:27] Marco: let's talk the bench plan briefly. Ethan, can you outline what you'll measure?
[07:32] Ethan: sure. plan is: 1) baseline latency and cost with normal KMS and full model, 2) simulate KMS revocation — route traffic to cache-only + degraded model variant, measure 95/99 latencies and error rates, 3) run ramp tests for burst scenarios to validate autoscale thresholds, 4) capture token counts and cost delta. we'll provide a spreadsheet with expected numbers.
[07:58] Aisha: that sounds good. include a column for regulator-friendly metrics (time-to-serve, number of audited requests, verified signature).
[08:08] Maya: we'll also provide a short SOP for the on-call steps to flip the fallback and how to verify logs are being exported correctly.

[08:18] Lisa: one more ask — auditors want proof of role-based access control to logs, and that log deletion requires multi-approval. do you support RBAC and deletion locks?
[08:29] Ethan: yes, RBAC is in Console; deletions go through a workflow and we can require 2 approvals for deletion in Dedicated/Private. Hosted has configurable retention windows but for immutable deletion locks you'd want Dedicated or Private.
[08:45] Thomas: so the vendor-hosted option can meet some asks but not all; seems like Dedicated or Private is safer for us. what's the delta to move to Dedicated for us?
[08:55] Maya: delta is mainly contractual and capacity planning. Dedicated gives you customer-isolated GPU pools, region pinning, and full control of KMS. we can run a pricing/throughput estimate as part of the sprint.
[09:08] Marco: does Dedicated require a long term commit?
[09:11] Maya: typically yes, monthly or annual reserved capacity; but for the pilot we can propose a temporary pilot arrangement with limited commit. we'll put that in the pilot proposal.

[09:22] (slight crosstalk)
[09:28] Marco: thinking about the cache again — what about cache poisoning risks? auditors worry that cached content could be polluted.
[09:36] Ethan: good point. we have signature checks and can namespace caches per-tenant, and TTLs plus write-once flags for certain keys. for high-risk flows, we mark cache entries as read-only and only allow sanitized population. we'll include these mitigations in the tech doc.

[09:51] Lisa: can you show an example of cache metadata — like last-write, hash of input, scrubbed flag — in the export?
[09:58] Ethan: yes, we'll produce a small sample export showing those fields.

[10:05] Aisha: All right. let's recap next steps briefly.
[10:09] Maya: recap: Redwood sends SOC2 excerpt + architecture diagram + vendor HSM attestation by 2026-01-18. Redwood prepares bench plan and spreadsheet by 2026-01-22. Customer to sign NDA addendum by 2026-01-20 to allow Redwood repo access. Sprint proposed Feb 2 start, run two weeks, deliver audit-proof artifacts before Feb 10.
[10:32] Thomas: agreed. also include a short executive summary that we can present to our compliance board.
[10:38] Maya: will do.

[10:42] Lisa: thanks everyone. quick note — please mark any PII in exports as redacted; auditors will expect that.
[10:49] Ethan: we'll sanitize and include redaction step in the SOP.

[10:55] (end of meeting wrap, some small talk)
[11:10] Maya: thanks all, we'll follow up with links.

References shared: 1) link: https://redwood.example.com/sec-pack (SOC2 excerpt, internal) 2) bench plan stub: https://docs.redwood/benchmarks/crescendo-kv-bench (access controlled)

Notes on transcript quality: multiple short interruptions, occasional mis-heard words ("K-V cash" for KV cache) in the automated transcript.

End of transcript.
